name: Woolston Hennebique reinforced-concrete construction
description: A reinforced-concrete system associated with François Hennebique was used in the structure of Woolston Quay, Southampton.

date.basis: The source reports the date for this scoped event or archaeological context.

events.statement: The museum dates the Woolston Quay reinforced-concrete section to 1899.

evidence.supports: The museum dates this Woolston section to 1899 and says Mouchel introduced Hennebique’s French system under licence to Britain at Swansea in 1897; it does not document the Woolston contract.
The source attributes this contribution to francois-hennebique.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated case currently researched, not a claim of the capability’s original invention or global priority.

caveats: The surviving section is evidence of this specific construction; its detailed reinforcement and actual loads need construction records. The museum identifies Mouchel’s licensed 1897 Swansea introduction as background to the system, but does not establish the Woolston project’s contract or its cement supplier.

research.note: Independent depth review checked the museum object description: the Woolston section is dated 1899, while Mouchel’s licensed 1897 Swansea work is background, not evidence of the Woolston contract.
